analysis.title: GS Johnstone - GS TMT SPEC SALES: Sage beat & raise, Besi +ve, Airtel Mobile initiation, PANW beat & raise, Prosus/Tencent, ASML from road, DISH (19 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities faded early gains on 19 Nov. Nvidia closed down 3% after rising 2% pre-market despite a beat and raise. QQQ finished up 0.4% and semis up 0.3%, giving back most of a 1.5% opening gain and the 4% post-Nvidia rally.
Desk flows in Nvidia showed hedge-fund buying and short covering against continued long-only selling. The desk says that with this much uncertainty it is hard to see real sponsorship.

Rotation supported hyperscalers (Amazon +3%, Alphabet +1%), with a possible proxy trade noted. Consumer names rallied (TGT +5%, TJX +9%, LOW +70bps despite a miss). Retailers had a top-5 session YTD, and the desk attributes part of it to an unwind of consumer being among the most net sold sectors month to date.

The derivatives team says the S&P is in a spot-down, vol-down pattern. Volatility compressed after VIX expiry and Nvidia earnings without equities getting a meaningful bid, which the desk calls a more concerning shift from earlier in the week.

Floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale. Asset manager flows were modestly muted, hedge funds were small net buyers driven by macro products, and no sector skews materially net for sale. ETFs were 35% of the tape against a 28% YTD average.
Investor feedback from Barcelona: mood is described as quite dour. Telcos are solid as expected, except Sunrise, which again got the inorganic question. Software feedback is more mixed.

Wolters Kluwer moved lower even though its meetings were seen as solid. The desk points to recent long-only supply, broad software weakness, a possible large equity raise and renewed AI risk questions.

Sage beat and raised. Quarterly organic growth was 10% against consensus 8.7%, organic recurring growth 10.6% against 9.3%, and ARR growth 10.8% against 10.3%. Margin was 10.3%, in line. Guidance of growth in the region of 10% is above consensus of 9.4% and better than the 9-10% most investors expected.

Palo Alto Networks reported a strong 1QFY27. Revenue was 4% above Street, NGS ARR 2% above, EPS 8% ahead, with about a 140bp EBIT margin beat. FY27 revenue and NGS ARR guidance were raised and the shares rose about 8% after hours following a 10% regular-session gain. RPO, operating margin and FCF margin guidance were maintained.

GS sees PANW's $4.5bn Applied Compute acquisition as attaching the company more directly to AI token consumption across inference, observability and Prisma AIRS. It frames the print as reinforcing the platform-consolidation thesis.
Palo Alto management said agentic traffic is up about 9x yoy and that AI demand remains insatiable, with industry token revenue on a trajectory to surpass $1 trillion by 2029.

Tencent 3Q26 missed. Revenue was 2% below expectations, gross profit 3% below, operating profit 6% below and capex about 24% above Street. Weaker gaming (softer international games) and higher AI spending pressured results, and Prosus fell. GIR cut adjusted net profit forecasts for 4Q26, FY27 and FY28 by 5%, 11% and 11%.

GIR expects FY27 to be the EPS trough for Tencent and sees a near-trough 12x P/E as support after a c.40% YTD share decline. Management said capex intensity is peaking and compute prepayments should decline now that long-term memory contracts are secured.

Airtel Mobile Commerce was initiated at Neutral with a 260p price target. GS expects Airtel Money to deliver about 26% revenue ex-FX CAGR over FY26-31E, but sees balanced risk/reward given EM/FX volatility, rising competition and potential margin pressure.

ASML: GS reiterates Buy after the Wilton investor tour. High NA fleet availability is 87%, targeting 90% by year-end and 93% in 2028, with 13 tools expected in operation by year-end. ASML plans to raise EUV and immersion capacity 30% in 2027 and 2028. GS views Match Act concerns as overdone, with meaningful effects unlikely before 2028.

Besi: SK Hynix brought a Besi hybrid bonding tool, alongside a Hanwha tool, into Cheongju to test 20-layer HBM5 stacks, targeting mass production around 2028. GS calls it a small positive and a technology-path confirmation, but dual-source testing rather than a production commitment, and the transition has slipped before. It is not a near-term order catalyst.

Intel announced a debut external customer for its 18A-P process at 70% yields and named Microsoft as first public customer for EMIB advanced packaging. GS reads this as commercial traction for the foundry turnaround that does not immediately fix its financial challenges.

Nvidia expanded supply chain cooperation with TSMC, Hon Hai, ASE/SPIL, KYEC, Kinsus and Unimicron. Procurement commitments rose to US$390bn in 3Q and Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPU began mass-production shipments. Nvidia is reportedly investing more than US$1bn in Kinsus for substrate capacity. Senior TSMC management reportedly visited Nvidia HQ to reaffirm orders, unconfirmed by either company.

Broadcom earnings preview: GS expects investors to focus on FY27 guidance confidence, datacenter and customer readiness for FY28 deployments, and competition from MediaTek. Expectations are muted and GS expects modest upside to guidance, with the stock driven by clarity on AI spending sustainability into 2028.

The ECB's November 2026 Financial Stability Review warned that the debt-fuelled AI investment boom has historical parallels with the dotcom and subprime bubbles. It estimates major tech companies accumulated more than $4 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments by end of Q2 2026.

GS 2027 Global Credit Outlook expects modest spread widening in IG and HY, a slight preference for USD over EUR in IG, higher issuance driven by AI funding, M&A and maturity walls, modest HY underperformance versus IG in USD, bifurcation between AI-related issuers and the rest, friendlier duration and modestly higher defaults.

Dish Wireless agreed a $525m settlement with American Tower over its abandoned 5G network and is negotiating similar deals with other creditors including Charter. Funds come from a $2.4bn creditor trust and need FCC approval by year-end. Crown Castle, with the largest claim at about $3.5bn, said Dish had not approached it.

Citi, JPMorgan, Bank of America, PNC and Citizens say customers are responsible for activity by third-party AI agents they allow into their accounts, per TechCrunch. This creates a trust barrier for AI firms entering personal finance, and banks also face a competitive threat from agents that help customers avoid fees and low-interest deposits.

Several advertisers in Spain, including Santander, paused TikTok activity over concerns about CSAM circulating on the platform. Italy is set to restrict youth social media access, with a decree banning under-13s expected by year-end.

market_movers.rationale: Shares closed down 3% after a beat and raise, with hedge-fund buying and short covering offset by continued long-only selling.
1QFY27 beat on revenue, NGS ARR, EPS and EBIT margin, with FY27 revenue and NGS ARR guidance raised. Shares rose about 8% after hours.
GS reiterates Buy after the Wilton visit on High NA progress, competitive moat and output and services upside. Match Act concerns are seen as overdone.
Airtel Mobile Commerce initiated at Neutral. Strong growth and cash conversion are balanced by EM/FX volatility, competition and margin pressure.
Sage beat on organic growth, recurring growth and ARR growth, and guided to about 10% growth against 9.4% consensus.
3Q26 missed on revenue and operating profit with capex well above Street. GIR cut profit forecasts and expects FY27 to be the EPS trough.
Besi tool is in SK Hynix testing for 20-layer HBM5 stacks. A small positive, but dual-source testing and not a near-term order catalyst.
Debut external 18A-P customer at 70% yields and Microsoft as first public EMIB packaging customer show foundry traction.
Earnings preview expects modest upside to guidance with muted expectations. Stock driven by AI spending sustainability into 2028.

sector_views.rationale: Retailers had a top-5 session YTD, partly a positioning unwind after consumer was among the most net sold sectors month to date.
Investor feedback is more mixed, with broad weakness and questions about the risk of AI.
Investor feedback on telcos is pretty solid as expected, with Sunrise facing inorganic questions again.

earnings_insights: Sage (reported, morning of 19 Nov): quarterly organic growth 10% vs consensus 8.7%, organic recurring growth 10.6% vs consensus 9.3%, ARR growth 10.8% vs consensus 10.3%, margin 10.3% in line. FY guidance of growth in the region of 10% vs consensus 9.4%.

Palo Alto Networks 1QFY27 (reported 19 Nov after close): revenue 4% above Street, NGS ARR 2% above, EPS 8% ahead, EBIT margin about 140bp above. FY27 revenue and NGS ARR guidance raised, FY RPO, operating margin and FCF margin guidance maintained.

Tencent 3Q26 (reported): revenue 2% below expectations, gross profit 3% below, operating profit 6% below, capex about 24% above Street. Revenue grew 8% yoy and operating profit fell 6%, 2ppts and 6ppts below GS estimates. GIR cut adjusted net profit forecasts for 4Q26/FY27/FY28 by 5%/11%/11%.
Nvidia (reported 18 Nov after close): beat expectations and raised guidance, shares closed down 3% on 19 Nov.
Target, TJX and Lowe's (reported): TGT +5%, TJX +9% and LOW +70bps despite a miss, per the desk.
Broadcom (preview, not yet reported): GS expects modest upside to guidance, with focus on FY27 guidance, FY28 deployment readiness and competition from MediaTek.
risk_factors: Weak investor confidence, with many waiting for clarity and for faster progress at frontier AI labs.
Sustainability of AI infrastructure spending into 2028, including land, power and shell constraints and external funding concerns for emerging hyperscalers.
ECB warning of dotcom and subprime parallels in the debt-funded AI investment boom and more than $4 trillion of tech off-balance-sheet commitments.
AI disruption risk for software names and a possible large equity raise.
Slowing core growth, rising AI investment and record capex and compute prepayments driving free cash flow outflows at Tencent.
Slippage risk in the HBM hybrid bonding transition, which has slipped before.
Modest credit spread widening and rising defaults expected in 2027.
Banks refusing liability for AI agent transactions creates a trust barrier for agent-based personal finance.
vol_and_positioning: S&P traded in a spot-down, vol-down regime on 19 Nov. After clearing VIX expiry and Nvidia earnings, vol compressed across the board without equities catching a meaningful bid.
Nvidia desk flows: hedge-fund buying and covering against continued long-only supply, consistent with after-hours flows the prior night.
Floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, hedge funds screened small net buyers driven by macro products, and no sector skews materially net for sale.
ETF share of tape is 35% against a 28% YTD average.
Consumer has been among the most net sold sectors month to date per the GS prime brokerage update, so the retailer rally partly reflects a positioning unwind.
geopolitical: Match Act concerns over restrictions on DUV and immersion lithography shipments to China, which GS says depend on implementation beyond the US and are unlikely to have meaningful effects before 2028.

tension_points.bear_case: Shares reversed from +2% pre-market to -3% on continued long-only selling, and vol fell without equities getting a bid, which the desk calls a more concerning shift. The desk says it is hard to see real sponsorship while uncertainty persists.
